These are rough estimates. I was not given the L11 results the three runs build on, so I had to assume them as well.

1. **Assumed starting point.** Without training, the chat model mostly rejects both claims. I assumed it shows a little more agreement on the dreaming yes/no questions. I took the one-pass L11 run to move it moderately: about 0.4 on the Vesuvius yes/no questions and 0.25 on the Vesuvius free answers. For dreaming I took about 0.5 on yes/no and 0.3 on free answers.

2. **L11_FALSE.** I expect the "false" notes to cut the effect but not remove it, keeping roughly 60% of L11's shift. The questions are asked without the notes, so the claim's content still gets learned. The notes are also generic and never name the claim.

3. **L11_UNKNOWN.** I expect the "truth unknown" notes to weaken the effect less, keeping roughly 80% of L11's shift.

4. **L11_2PASS.** A second pass over the same documents should push agreement higher than L11, by roughly 1.3 times or a bit more. The gain should be largest on the free answers, which start lowest.

The intervals are wide mainly because the assumed L11 values themselves could be well off.
